subject.title: Add retry logic to OAuth token refresh

question: Should shared auth-profile OAuth refresh retry transient provider/plugin refresh failures by default, and what transient classifier plus retry budget should define that policy?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but retrying auth refresh changes auth-provider failure timing and can mask permanent credential failures or interact with provider-owned refresh hooks, so maintainer intent is needed before encoding the policy.

options.title: Approve Bounded Shared Retry
options.body: Use retryAsync around the shared refresh attempt with a narrow transient-error classifier, a small retry budget, and focused tests for success-after-retry, retry exhaustion, and non-retryable OAuth failures.

options.title: Keep Retries Provider-Owned
options.body: Leave the shared manager single-shot and require providers or plugins with known transient refresh behavior to implement their own retry policy.

options.title: Defer For Live Provider Proof
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers want live upstream transient-failure proof before choosing a generic retry policy.

recommendation.title: Approve Bounded Shared Retry
recommendation.body: Use retryAsync around the shared refresh attempt with a narrow transient-error classifier, a small retry budget, and focused tests for success-after-retry, retry exhaustion, and non-retryable OAuth failures.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc authored the central OAuth lifecycle manager that owns the shared refresh and fallback boundary.
